findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` as abstract (pre-existing) and this PR adds a new abstract method `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. None of these are implemented by MetricAlertDetectorHandler. Since StatefulDetectorHandler is an abc.ABC with these as @abc.abstractmethod, attempting to instantiate MetricAlertDetectorHandler (e.g. via `Detector.detector_handler` -> `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for any Detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Previously this class was a concrete (if no-op) DetectorHandler subclass that worked fine; this change silently turns it into a landmine that crashes at runtime the moment it's used.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring not updated for new dict return type
findings.body: The docstring for StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate() still says 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method signature and implementation now return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, not a list. This is left over from before the API change described in the PR and is now inaccurate, which can mislead future readers/maintainers about the actual return type/shape.

findings.title: No test exercises instantiation of the changed MetricAlertDetectorHandler
findings.body: This PR changes MetricAlertDetectorHandler to subclass StatefulDetectorHandler (previously DetectorHandler) without providing the newly-required abstract method implementations. No test in this PR (or referenced in the diff) instantiates MetricAlertDetectorHandler or exercises `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler(detector)` / `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector of type `metric_alert_fire`. Such a test would have caught the TypeError raised when trying to instantiate this now-abstract class, so this regression was not caught by the test suite included in the PR.
